summary: Rabbi Tawil discusses the conquest of Yericho in the book of Yehoshua, focusing on the recurring motif of the number seven and the necessity of relinquishing control to Hashem. He explores the concept of cherem, where the spoils of war are consecrated to Hashem, and examines the role of the prophet in establishing decrees that Hashem upholds.
questions: Why does the number seven appear so frequently in the Torah and in the battle of Yericho?
What is the significance of the Jewish people circling the city of Yericho for seven days?
Why did Yehoshua forbid the people from taking any spoils from the city of Yericho?
How does the story of the man in the desert relate to the human struggle for control?
Can a prophet make a decree that Hashem will uphold even if it was not explicitly commanded?
